one_liner: Hybrid instrumentation plus sampling frame profiler for C/C++ with nanosecond rdtsc timestamps and a remote GUI; no measured win over perf, gprof or Valgrind.
what_it_does: Tracy records manually marked zones (ZoneScoped and related macros from public/tracy/Tracy.hpp), frames, locks, plots, messages, memory allocations, GPU zones (OpenGL, Vulkan, D3D11/12, Metal, OpenCL, CUDA, WebGPU, ROCm) and context switches, and can also sample call stacks without markup. The profiled program (client) compiles in public/TracyClient.cpp and streams events over TCP to a separate viewer or capture tool (server), which shows a live timeline, statistics and source/assembly views. It is not a drop-in for perf or gprof: zones need source macros and a TRACY_ENABLE build; without the define all macros compile out.
how_it_is_fast: Each zone begin/end writes a 32-byte item into a thread-local 128-item queue buffer with an inline rdtsc timestamp and a pointer to a static source-location struct; the manual's x64 listing shows about 20 instructions and no locks on the hot path. Heavy work (string resolution, compression, symbol lookup) is deferred to a background thread and to the server, which also reduces network bandwidth.
when_to_use: Games and other frame-based real-time apps where you need to see which frame stuttered and why, across threads, not just aggregate hot spots
Native C/C++ (also C API, Lua, Python, Fortran) code you can rebuild with TRACY_ENABLE and zone macros
Profiling on a remote or mobile device (Android, iOS, consoles via platform layer) with the viewer on a desktop
Correlating CPU zones with GPU work, lock contention, allocations and context switches in one timeline
Long captures with millions of zones where per-event cost of tens of ns is acceptable
when_not_to_use: You cannot rebuild or annotate the binary and only want whole-program sampling: perf or a pure sampler needs no build change
Very fine-grained zones (sub-100 ns functions) where an event cost of roughly 25-30 ns per zone (issue #192; derived figure below) distorts what you measure
Virtual machines or cloud instances: the manual warns of reduced timestamp precision and missing invariant TSC
macOS/iOS: the manual says the overhead is higher, TRACY_NO_EXIT is unsupported and OpenGL cannot be profiled
Hard limits matter: 65534 source locations, 64 threads per lock, 1.6-day sessions, 16 million unique call stacks, little-endian 48-bit address space only

integration.form: source-drop (add public/TracyClient.cpp, or CMake/Meson target Tracy::TracyClient as static or shared lib); viewer is a separate CMake-built app
integration.dependencies: client: none beyond pthread and libdl on Unix (libexecinfo on BSD; optional libunwind, libdebuginfod); server build needs network and git at CMake configure time to fetch its libraries
integration.min_toolchain: C++11; MSVC, GCC or Clang (MSVC Edit and Continue /ZI must be off)
integration.platforms: Windows (x86, x64, ARM64), Linux (x86, x64, ARM, ARM64), Android, FreeBSD, WSL, macOS x64, iOS, QNX; x86 needs invariant rdtsc (Sandy Bridge or later); little-endian only
integration.thread_safety: Client zones are recorded into per-thread queues and are safe from any thread; lock markup supports up to 64 threads per lock. dbghelp Sym* calls on Windows must be serialized with Tracy's (manual).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — sampling works without markup, but the main instrumentation mode needs TRACY_ENABLE builds and source macros, unlike perf/gprof

gotchas: The manual's 2.25 ns per zone is wall-clock difference divided by zones while 12 threads ran in parallel; per-thread cost is about 12x that, roughly 27 ns per zone (derived from page data), which matches the 28-29 ns per span a user measured on a Ryzen 9 3950X with GCC 9.3 -O3 -flto -march=native (issue #192, open, rdtsc about 70% of time).
Without TRACY_ON_DEMAND the client buffers all events in memory until a viewer connects and never releases that memory (can reach gigabytes); on-demand mode adds bookkeeping cost per event.
TRACY_ENABLE must be defined for every translation unit; TRACY_ENABLE=0 still enables it because only definedness is checked.

ON_DEMAND with a static TracyLockable deadlocked during static initialization (issue #775, closed); the client also listens on all interfaces and broadcasts on the LAN by default (TRACY_ONLY_LOCALHOST, TRACY_NO_BROADCAST).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Tracy over Palanteer or MicroProfiler when you need GPU zones, broad platform coverage and a mature viewer; pick funtrace when you want automatic function-level tracing under 10 ns per call, and magic-trace or perf when you cannot add instrumentation.
verified_claims_summary: First-party manual table: etcpak compressing a 16384x16384 image on 12 threads with the 4x4 block function instrumented (16777216 zones per image) took 110.9 vs 148.2 ms (ETC1) and 212.4 vs 250.5 ms (ETC2) clean versus profiled, which the manual reports as 2.25 ns per zone; compiler, flags and CPU are not stated and no other profiler was measured. Because the division uses wall time across 12 parallel threads, the per-thread cost is closer to 27 ns per zone (derived from page data), consistent with an independent 28-29 ns report.
status_note: Very actively maintained (commits in October 2026, 16.9k stars), BSD-3-Clause and copyable; the master branch is the development line with no stability guarantee, so pin a release tag and keep client and viewer versions matched because the network protocol changes between releases.
